A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoLA research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable matching of retained and added material.

before.justification: V1 reports original vision-language and audio-visual experiments, component ablations, and computational measurements in Tables 1–6 and Figure 6.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds AVE experiments on compression, rank allocation, and adaptation directionality in Tables 7 and 11.

M1.justification: The original dual-path CoLA architecture and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Section 5.4 adds optional variants that generate Kronecker factors instead of the full fusion matrix and allocate unequal ranks to the intra-modal and inter-modal pathways.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate REC/RES on RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, and RefCOCOg, and audio-visual tasks on AVE and AVSBench-S4. The new experiments reuse AVE without introducing different data coverage or task requirements.

E2.justification: Tables 1–4 retain the same rank- and parameter-matched LoRA baselines and task-specific comparator sets. The added experiments reuse LoRA and examine internal CoLA variants; the newly cited foundation models are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Existing splits, metrics, backbones, and Appendix A training settings are retained. New AVE experiments introduce full versus factorized fusion outputs, intra/inter ranks of 16/16 versus 8/32, and directional controls that use standard LoRA in the encoder without cross-modal adaptation.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained sharing, propagation, and scaling-factor analyses, Section 5.4 and Appendices C.3–C.4 investigate compression, asymmetric rank allocation, unidirectional versus bidirectional adaptation, and hypernetwork parameter scaling. This substantially expands the analysis of CoLA’s design and scalability.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Reported averages concern task or dataset-split performance, not uncertainty across runs.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 and the existing plots retain their results. New AVE entries report 79.9 accuracy for symmetric Kronecker CoLA and 81.44 for intra/inter ranks 8/32; directional variants score 79.6 and 80.2 in Table 11. Table 12 adds parameter-cost results. These are additional configurations, not revised original benchmark scores.

T1.justification: V2 adds Section 3.3’s per-input rank bound, vectorization and Kronecker-rank derivation, Theorem 3.1 bounding the span of input-dependent updates, and pathway-gradient derivations. Section 5.4 also introduces a Kronecker formulation. V1 contains no corresponding theoretical analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about cross-modal low-rank adaptation, multimodal performance, and the first multi-task PEFT framework for visual grounding. The added analyses support these retained claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations connecting dynamic fusion to input-dependent expressive capacity and separate parameters to gradient structure. It interprets the new ablations as supporting bidirectional interaction and greater inter-modal rank allocation, and attributes the remaining measured inference overhead specifically to the inter-modal pathway.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-availability link, hypernetwork parameter breakdowns, and explicit disclosure that CoLA’s intra-modal weights were merged for Figure 6’s inference comparison. Appendix C’s blanket statement linking all ablations to the vision-language training settings is removed; Appendix A’s actual hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds DINOv3, CG-SSL, and BEATs as examples of unimodal foundation models. The broader research positioning remains unchanged. Other reference changes mainly update publication metadata for already cited works.

P1.justification: Existing prose and the overall section sequence are largely retained, with localized subsection additions and explanatory annotations. Sara Ahmed becomes Sara Atito in the author list, the publication footer changes, and several bibliography entries are edited.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 7, 11, and 12 and renumbers the retained training tables. Existing figures and tables undergo limited relocation and page reflow, including Figure 6 moving to a separate page. The six existing figures retain their plotted or diagrammatic content.

improvement.justification: The added rank/expressivity analysis, directional controls, compression experiments, and implementation disclosures strengthen explanation and support for the retained work. The gains are qualified by an inconsistency in Section 5.4: its stated mn+pq formula implies 64 outputs at rank 32, whereas Table 7 reports 80. This weakens the new compression description but leaves the retained evidence and other additions intact.
